CharacterStyleRange.Content: Due to a combination of macroeconomic and regulatory factors, wagering turnover on VTR fell by 4.0% year-on-year in FY25.

In addition, wagering service providers (WSPs) were required to absorb the cost of a 50% increase in the Point of Consumption Tax (PoCT), which rose from 10% to 15% on 1 July 2024. WSPs responded to this PoCT increase by offering less competitive betting markets and by decreasing their spend on customer generosities (free bet turnover was down by 6% year-on-year), both of which had a negative impact on turnover.

Despite these headwinds, data provided by WSPs shows that VTR attracted turnover from more than 1.3 million digital customers in FY25 and continues to see customer growth. Turnover remains 8.4% above FY19, which was the final year prior to COVID lockdowns.
After a challenging first half of the year, which saw turnover decline by 6.6% year-on-year, the second half of FY25 saw a stabilisation with a minimal decrease of 0.1% year-on-year.
Notwithstanding the soft overall performance in H1, feature meetings held during the Spring Racing Carnival continued to perform strongly:

• The Manikato Stakes was added to AFL Grand Final eve at The Valley and proved an instant success with meeting turnover up by 18% year-on-year (noting that the Group 1 Moir Stakes featured on the program in 2023). The 2024 Grand Final long weekend was a hit across the board, with turnover on the Benalla Cup meeting on Friday afternoon up 4.7% and Saturday’s Sandown Stakes meeting up a huge 47.6%.

• Turnover was consistent with the previous year across the Country Cup meetings run during spring, significantly defying the broader wagering trends and underscoring the importance of country racing to the industry.

• The four-day Melbourne Cup Carnival again underpinned its importance to the Victorian racing industry, accounting for 8.8% of total turnover across FY25 and featuring three of the top five turnover races in Victoria:

The second half of the year saw a significant improvement in year-on-year performance, aided by softer benchmarks from the previous year and two cash rate decreases announced by the Royal Bank of Australia (RBA), which increased disposable income and therefore wagering turnover.

The revamped Festival of Racing was embraced by punters, with turnover on feature metropolitan meetings and Country Cups across the period (from 8 February to 29 March 2025) increasing by 1.1% year-on-year.

The third edition of the Sportsbet Future Stars Series was successfully held across January and February, with competitive heats averaging 10.7 starters per race (up from 10.0 in 2024). Race turnover across the entire series remained strong, averaging $1.8m (up by 5% year-on-year) which is well above the average turnover for country premium maidens across the same period. Notably, turnover on the Future Stars Final delivered substantial year-on-year growth (68%), again underscoring the success of the series and strong customer engagement.
FY25 marked a significant change in RV’s wagering income model, following the conclusion of the Tabcorp Joint Venture at the end of FY24 (the final settlement payment was made in early FY25).

To ensure the stable funding of the industry, RV entered a new agreement with the Victorian State Government to deliver compensation for the increased PoCT, which disproportionately impacts racing relative to other codes.

Changes to the race fields fees model were introduced in October 2024 following extensive consultation with WSPs and Victorian bookmakers. While race fields fees declined by 8.5% year-on-year, this was primarily due to results impacting the WSP’s margins rather than any change to the race fields model, which delivered a 2% increase in race fields fees relative to the previous model.
